subject: [ESCALATION] NorthCentra — EastUS1 latency & error surge / emergency routing handoff
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:12:00Z
Subject: Fwd: [NorthCentra] Severe latency + 5xx spike — EastUS1

Forwarding an alert from NorthCentra SRE. Customer seeing sustained p95/p99 latency blowups and a sharp rise in 5xxs starting 07:45 UTC. Impacting their API (ingest and realtime inference paths). They report a throughput drop and request urgent remediation and an ETA.

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Alice Chen <alice@northcentra.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-22T07:55:00Z
Subject: Severe latency + 5xx spike — EastUS1

Hi Ben,

We started seeing a latency surge at ~07:45 UTC in EastUS1. P95 for generation requests shot from ~350ms to >2s and 5xx rate jumped to ~8%. Throughput also dropped ~30% as retries pile up. This is customer-facing for several of our enterprise clients. Can Redwood advise next steps and ETA to stabilize? We need an owner for the remediation timeline and access to logs (requesting recent routing logs & KV cache traces).

Attached: summary.csv (small)

Thanks,
Alice
SRE, NorthCentra
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: [NorthCentra] Severe latency + 5xx spike — EastUS1

Thanks Ben + Alice. Copying infra and leadership. Quick triage notes and proposed actions: 

- Symptoms: p95/p99 latency and 5xx spike in EastUS1 starting ~07:45 UTC; throughput down ~30%. Customer also requests routing logs & KV cache traces.
- Hypothesis: regional AZ network flapping causing controller-driven KV cache invalidations (we've seen similar with aggressive prefix eviction under cross-AZ packet loss).
- Immediate mitigation (ask): perform a controlled traffic handoff: canary 20% to WestUS2, monitor for 15m, then ramp to 60-80% if metrics improve. Use smart-routing fallback (policy: prefer ring2 WestUS2, allow cold-start of WestUS2 model variant if needed).
- Tactical owner: Hannah to execute reroute and collect traces. Jordan to keep rollback path ready. Marissa — can you approve a customer-facing incident note + a credit conversation if we need to offer one?

Please execute the canary ASAP and post updates in this thread. I will prepare an exec note for the CSM and our leadership once we have telemetry.

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T08:25:00Z
Subject: ACTION: canary reroute initiated — EastUS1 -> WestUS2

On it — starting canary now. Steps I'm taking:

1) Apply routing policy patch (smart-routing) to prefer WestUS2 for NorthCentra route. Patch: runbook-routing-patch.diff (small change to weight + cooldown).
2) Move 20% traffic to WestUS2 (canary).
3) Enable verbose KV cache logging for the affected model and capture kvcache snapshots.
4) Export routing logs to S3 /incident-traces/northcentra/2027-05-22/ for customer download.

I'll monitor p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, and throughput. If we see >50% improvement in 15m, I'll ramp to 60%. Jordan — please keep the rollback (drain) playbook ready.

Attachments: runbook-routing-patch.diff (patch applied)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T11:05:00Z
Subject: Update: canary -> ramp / metrics show improvement

Status update (11:05 UTC):

- Canary was initiated at 08:25 UTC. At 08:40 we saw early improvements and started ramping at 08:50. Ramp to ~70% completed by 10:45 UTC.
- Metrics (comparison pre-mitigation -> now): p95 latency: 2.1s -> 380ms; 5xx rate: 8.5% -> 0.8%; throughput recovered to ~92% of baseline.
- Actions performed: routing weight adjustments, KV cache snapshot (attached), exported routing logs to https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/2027-05-22-nc-eastus1.
- Attachments: incident-dashboard.png (dashboard screenshot), network-trace.zip (tcpdump + traces), runbook-routing-patch.diff

Next steps:
- Continue monitoring for 6 hours with 70% WestUS2 traffic.
- Postmortem: collect model-internal cache eviction traces and control-plane event logs (Jordan lead).
- Customer comms: Marissa, please prepare a short note confirming stabilization and offer for a follow-up RCA + possible credit (per deal NC-3472).

If we see reversion, we'll execute a full region drain to WestUS2 (pre-approved by me).

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T15:04:00Z
Subject: Exec summary / next steps — NorthCentra EastUS1 incident

Quick executive summary for leadership:

- What happened: EastUS1 saw AZ-level network instability at ~07:45 UTC triggering elevated packet loss and controller-side kv-cache churn. That caused sustained p95/p99 latency increases and an elevated 5xx rate for NorthCentra traffic.
- Impact: Customer-facing latency and transient failures; throughput reduced ~30% before mitigation. High-touch account (NC-3472) — potential for credit/AM escalation.
- Mitigation taken: Controlled canary -> ramped to 70% WestUS2. Current metrics: p95 ~380ms, 5xx ~0.8%, throughput ~92% baseline.
- Root-cause hypothesis: AZ network flapping + aggressive cache invalidation policy.
- Follow-ups: Jordan to run postmortem (JIRA INF-4217) and validate controller cooldown thresholds; Hannah to correlate kvcache snapshots with controller events; Marissa to draft customer stabilization note and credit recommendation.
- Ask of leadership: approve up to 10% service credit for NC-3472 pre-approval to speed resolution if customer requests, and sign-off for a hosted-notice if we detect any reversion.

I'll sync with Marissa and the CSM to finalize comms. Full postmortem due EOD +48.

Rishi
VP, Infrastructure & Operations
Redwood Inference
